# a-default-scope-is-the-widest-one

**Claim.** When a dangerous operation infers which targets it acts on, the inferred set is the widest one available, and a guard computed by subtracting the operated set from that same source is empty exactly when the fallback fired.

**Not when.** Read-only operations where the widest scope costs only time · When the full set genuinely is the intended default, and it is small, named and shown before acting · When the inference draws on something narrower than the risk

**Check.** run the command with no scope argument: it refuses, and the "not reached" report is computed against the declared scope

*measured.* Open the full note only when you cannot tell whether its boundary holds here: [a-default-scope-is-the-widest-one](../notes/active/a-default-scope-is-the-widest-one.md).
